qs.situation: Your team asks for an invoice to be due 5 business days after Monday 6 October. Which days should be skipped when counting?
options: Only Saturdays and Sundays are skipped
Saturdays, Sundays and our listed public holidays are skipped (e.g. Diwali, Republic Day)
Sundays and public holidays are skipped, but Saturday is a working day for us

qs.situation: An order is placed on Saturday and promised '2 business days' later. Where does the counting begin?
options: Monday is day 1, so it is due Tuesday
Monday is day 0, so it is due Wednesday
Treat a weekend order as if it came in on Friday evening, so it is due Tuesday of the same week

qs.situation: Your financial year runs April to March. A sale is made on 15 May 2026. How should it be labelled?
options: FY2026-Q1 (the calendar year we start in, quarter counted from April)
FY2027-Q1 (named for the year the financial year ends)
Just Q1 with no year in the label

qs.situation: Sharma Traders owes ₹20,000 and pays 30 days late. How is the late fee worked out?
options: A one-time 1.5% of the invoice, ₹300, once it is overdue
1.5% for every month late, so it grows the longer they wait
A fixed ₹50 for each day late, no matter the invoice size

qs.situation: Mr Iyer pays an invoice 3 days after the due date. Does he pay a fee?
options: Yes, the fee applies from the first day late
No, the first 7 days late are free, fee starts after that
No, the first 15 days late are free, fee starts after that

qs.situation: A very small invoice of ₹100 is 10 days late, and a very large invoice of ₹10,00,000 is also late. Are there limits on the fee?
options: No limits, the fee is just the percentage (₹1.50 and ₹15,000 here)
There is a minimum fee of ₹50, so even small invoices pay at least that
There is a minimum of ₹50 and the fee never goes above ₹5,000

qs.situation: A customer has 5,000 points exactly. Which membership level are they?
options: Gold, the higher level (5,000 and above is Gold)
Silver, they need to go above 5,000 to reach Gold
It depends on how much they spent this year, not points alone

qs.situation: A customer returned a big order and their points balance dropped to minus 200. What level are they?
options: Lowest level (Bronze), they stay a member
No level at all, they lose membership until points are positive
They keep the level they had before the return

qs.situation: A receipt prints the card 4111 1111 1111 1234. What may the customer and staff see?
options: Only the last 4 digits, everything else hidden
The first 6 and last 4 digits, the middle hidden
Only the last 2 digits

qs.situation: Staff type a card number with only 3 digits, or with a letter in it, by mistake. What should the receipt show?
options: Hide everything, show nothing from what was typed
Refuse to print and show a warning to the staff member
Show whatever was typed so staff can spot the mistake

qs.situation: A staff member types the product code ' ab 123_x ' into the till. How should it be tidied up for the catalogue?
options: AB-123-X (trimmed, capitals, dashes in place of spaces and underscores)
AB123X (all spaces and dashes removed)
AB-123-X, plus always add our company prefix in front, such as KR-AB-123-X

qs.situation: A staff member types a code containing the letter O where the catalogue only has zeros (e.g. 'AB-1O0'), or leaves it blank. What happens?
options: Blank gives no code, odd characters are refused, and O is never silently swapped for 0
Letter O and zero, and letter I and one, are treated as the same and fixed automatically
Any code that doesn't match the catalogue is refused, including blank ones, with a message to staff

qs.situation: A customer scores the survey 6 out of 10. How do you count them?
options: Detractor (0 to 6 are detractors)
Passive (we treat 6 as neutral)
Detractor only up to 5, so 6 and 7 are passive and 8 and above promoters

qs.situation: A 1.2 kg parcel goes to Zone B. How is the price built up?
options: A base charge for the zone plus a set amount for each extra 500g, rounded up to the next 500g
A different fixed price for each weight band and zone, from our rate card
One flat price per zone regardless of weight, up to a limit

qs.situation: Someone enters a delivery zone we do not serve, a parcel of 0 g, or a 60 kg parcel. What should happen?
options: Unknown zone or zero weight is refused, but very heavy parcels are priced by the same rule
Unknown zone or zero weight is refused, and anything over 30 kg is also refused
Heavy parcels over 30 kg are accepted but charged as freight at a higher rate per kg

qs.situation: Four friends split a ₹1,000.10 bill at your restaurant. It cannot divide evenly. Who covers the leftover paise?
options: Everyone pays the same, rounded up, so the restaurant is never short (may collect a little extra)
Everyone pays the rounded-down amount and the restaurant absorbs the difference
Three pay the lower amount and one person (the first) pays the extra paise so the total is exact

qs.situation: A waiter enters a bill split between 0 people by mistake. What should happen?
options: Refuse with an error message
Treat it as 1 person, so the whole bill shows
Show no amount and leave it blank

qs.situation: Five orders in a group are worth ₹100, ₹200, ₹300 and ₹400. What is the 'middle value' of the four?
options: ₹250, the average of the two middle orders
₹200, the lower of the two middle orders
₹300, the higher of the two middle orders

qs.situation: A group of orders has some with the amount left blank, or every amount in the group is blank. What is the middle value?
options: Blanks are ignored, and a group with no amounts at all shows nothing
Blanks count as ₹0, and a group with no amounts shows ₹0
If any amount in the group is blank, no middle value is shown for that group
